svg.text: All nine inside for the night, HG3 last in by the gate
Door swing. Keep clear. 1988 mm headroom.
Lead-in line and traffic lane edge.
Vehicle stand outline and stand number.
Weighing and loading zone, cold chain.
600 mm working strip at every fitting.
1. Evening. The diagonal fills first, east to
2. Then the north rank, deepest first: N1
against the east wall, then N2, N3, N4.
3. HG3 comes in last and stands by the gate.
It is first out in the morning.
4. Both doors open on all eight Flagships once
they are in. HG3 has none.
5. Morning is this list read backwards: HG3
out, then N4, N3, N2, N1, then D1 to D4.
Nine vehicles inside for the night: eight
Flagships and HG3. This is Warehouse
Design V3 exactly as the model has it, not
The order is fixed, and it has to be. The
north rank stands nose to tail with 508 mm
between canopies, so it comes out
shallowest first; and HG3 parks across the
gate, so it moves before anything else
The diagonal's doors overlap. At a 3494 mm
pitch each door sweeps about 0.63 m2 over
the next canopy, and the top 21 mm of the
open door sits at canopy height. The leaf
itself clears by 55 mm - it is the upper
arm that fouls. Shutting one door lets the
neighbour out; dropping that arm 25 mm
would let them all stand open.
Two clearances are short. HG3 stops 101 mm
from the check-in desk, so check-in is
unusable while it is parked there, and the
north rank leaves 593 mm in front of the
crates where 600 is wanted. The fridges
Verified by driving it: every one of the
nine was planned out of the gate against
the others still standing, then replayed
pose by pose in exact geometry. Tightest
Geometry read directly from Hardware Designs/Warehouse Design V2.3dm and V3.3dm, 9 Sep 2026. Vehicle positions found from each vehicle's own three wheels. All dimensions in millimetres.
